Oppose his words - political criticism is your right - but not humiliating other people's sexuality. virals.hook:
🇶🇦 Qatar is trying to preserve the Iranian regime to continue extracting Iranian gas.
Qatar has become one of the main mediators in negotiations between the Islamic Republic of Iran and the United States. Many claim that it is precisely Qatar, through its paid lobby in the US, that is pressuring Trump to conclude a deal with the Iranian regime instead of taking more radical actions.

But why is this beneficial to Qatar?
1. Gas and economic interests
The world's largest gas field, "South Pars" (in Iran), or "North Dome" (in Qatar), is located in the territorial waters of both countries. Accordingly, Iran and Qatar extract gas from one common field.
According to estimates, by 2024, Qatar had extracted approximately 4 trillion cubic meters of gas from this field, while Iran had extracted approximately 2 trillion.
This is due to the fact that Iran started developing the field significantly later due to technological limitations and sanctions. In recent years, the regime has also faced a shortage of financing and technologies necessary to expand gas extraction and maintain pressure in the field.

If the regime changes in Iran and international sanctions are lifted, foreign companies will be able to invest billions of dollars in the Iranian gas industry.
In that case, Qatar, whose main income is linked to gas exports, will have to compete with Iran, which has huge natural gas reserves and broader geographical possibilities for its export.

It is in Qatar's interest to preserve the weak Islamic Republic under sanctions in order to continue enjoying its advantage in developing the common gas field.

2. Ideological and geopolitical interests
Qatar is closely linked to the Muslim Brotherhood organization, whose ideology is based on political Islam and the aspiration to build a society on Islamic principles.
In the event of a regime change in Iran, the Iranian people will send the 500-year-old institution of mullahs to the trash heap of history and return to their Iranian and pre-Islamic identity.
This could radically change the balance of power in the Middle East, and not in favor of states in which Islam plays a significant role in political life, such as Qatar, Pakistan, and Turkey.

outsiders.hook:

The Iranian American Legal Defense Fund (IALDF), which brought a lawsuit challenging the government's handling of confidential asylum information, deserves recognition for bringing these concerns into the open. Its Executive Director, Yasmine Chubin, and the organization's legal work are helping defend people who may face grave consequences if returned to Iran.
I know firsthand what it means to be held by the Islamic Republic. I spent 444 days as a hostage. I don't confuse the Iranian people with the regime that rules them. Nor should the American people.
America must not betray the trust of people who came here seeking protection. Asylum is a promise, not a bargaining chip.

outsiders.hook:
🇶🇦 Qatar is trying to preserve the Iranian regime to continue extracting Iranian gas.
Qatar has become one of the main mediators in negotiations between the Islamic Republic of Iran and the United States. Many claim that it is precisely Qatar, through its paid lobby in the US, that is pressuring Trump to conclude a deal with the Iranian regime instead of taking more radical actions.

But why is this beneficial to Qatar?
1. Gas and economic interests
The world's largest gas field, "South Pars" (in Iran), or "North Dome" (in Qatar), is located in the territorial waters of both countries. Accordingly, Iran and Qatar extract gas from one common field.
According to estimates, by 2024, Qatar had extracted approximately 4 trillion cubic meters of gas from this field, while Iran had extracted approximately 2 trillion.
This is due to the fact that Iran started developing the field significantly later due to technological limitations and sanctions. In recent years, the regime has also faced a shortage of financing and technologies necessary to expand gas extraction and maintain pressure in the field.

If the regime changes in Iran and international sanctions are lifted, foreign companies will be able to invest billions of dollars in the Iranian gas industry.
In that case, Qatar, whose main income is linked to gas exports, will have to compete with Iran, which has huge natural gas reserves and broader geographical possibilities for its export.

It is in Qatar's interest to preserve the weak Islamic Republic under sanctions in order to continue enjoying its advantage in developing the common gas field.

2. Ideological and geopolitical interests
Qatar is closely linked to the Muslim Brotherhood organization, whose ideology is based on political Islam and the aspiration to build a society on Islamic principles.
In the event of a regime change in Iran, the Iranian people will send the 500-year-old institution of mullahs to the trash heap of history and return to their Iranian and pre-Islamic identity.
This could radically change the balance of power in the Middle East, and not in favor of states in which Islam plays a significant role in political life, such as Qatar, Pakistan, and Turkey.
